thread:
maria: Heads up — after rolling kernel 6.1.12 on the GPU fleet, node_exporter is returning a bunch of scrape 403s for /proc/driver/nvidia and a few nodes are flapping out of our SLO alert. Prom is spiking with 5xx on target scrape.
kevin: seen it. dcgm-exporter also logging 'driver/sysfs permission denied' intermittently. Only the machines with the new kernel?
maria: yeah only the nodes in us-west2 that got the hotpatch last night. non-gpu nodes fine.
raj: quick ask — did kubelet change ProcMount behavior? I remember some kernels + container runtimes will mask parts of /proc unless procMount: Unmasked is set.
alex: we run node-exporter as a non-root user in the daemonset so that could be it. Historically it's been able to read /proc/driver/* but kernel/selinux changes can break that.
kevin: can we confirm with a check pod? sudo into a node and run:
```
kubectl debug node/us-west2-gpu-41 -it --image=registry.redwood/diag:latest --share-processes
ls -l /proc/driver/nvidia
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/0/information
```
maria: did that — ls shows owner root:root mode 600 on some files, previously they were 644. cat fails with permission denied when containerized. On host it's readable.
raj: short-term mitigation: we can patch the node-exporter daemonset to use procMount: Unmasked and run as root for the nodes in that cordon group. Long-term we should get the kernel vendor to explain why mask tightened.
kevin: patch example (tested on staging):
```
kubectl patch daemonset node-exporter -n monitoring --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/securityContext/procMount","value":"Unmasked"}]'
```
This makes node-exporter see the same /proc layout as host.
alex: note that some clusters disallow Unmasked by policy — POD security policies or OPA gate may block. We need a safe rollout plan.
maria: I'm for a canary: change DS on 2 nodes in us-west2 (label gpu-observability=canary), validate scraping, then roll. Also will add a readiness probe so Prom doesn't immediately mark it down during restart.
raj: also we should suppress the SRE alert noise: silence the alerting rule for node-exporter scrape errors for that region for 30m while we patch. I'll open a silence in Alertmanager.
infra-bot: @channel Alertmanager silence created by raj: 'node_exporter_scrape_errors us-west2' for 30m.
kevin: follow-up: after applying Unmasked we still saw DCGM exporter warnings on two nodes — turned out driver module was rebuilt against the old kernel headers. Repro steps to catch:
```
ssh node
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv
uname -r
```
If versions mismatch, the DCGM lib will error. We should add a node-exporter/diag metric check to SLO dashboard to catch driver/kernel mismatch as a preflight.
maria: good call. I'll add a lightweight prom rule to detect 'dcgm_exporter_up == 0 or node_driver_mismatch == 1' and wire it to the infra dashboard.
alex: and for the deployment playbook: 1) cordon nodes to roll, 2) patch DS with procMount Unmasked + temp runAsUser 0 for canary, 3) validate metrics for 10m, 4) roll remaining nodes, 5) revert runAsUser to non-root once kernel vendor gives guidance.
kevin: one more thing — cost/downtime note: the flapping caused 3x scrape retries and Prom ingest blew past our ingestion budget in us-west2. We should add rate-limits/backoff to the Prom job for node-exporter to avoid billing spikes during infra incidents.
raj: agreed. I'll open a ticket to add 'rate_limit: 200/s' and backoff on prometheus job config for node_exporter targets.
maria: ok I'm going to run the canary now and will post results here.
kevin: thanks — ping when done, we'll coordinate the silence expiry. :thumbsup:
(10 minutes later)
maria: canary looks green: node-exporter metrics resumed, no more 403s, dcgm exporter stable on canary nodes. rolling to remainder now.
alex: great, keep an eye on cost dashboard for unusual Prom spikes.
infra-bot: Deploy event: daemonset/node-exporter updated by maria at 1959991165.
maria: roll complete. created follow-ups: #1 tracking upstream kernel change, #2 add driver/kernel mismatch alert, #3 add procMount note to runbook.
kevin: closing the alert silence early.
raj: thanks everyone, good coordinated run.
